author: Yaqeen Advisory
title: What is a good MIS report? What to include and what to skip
summary: A good management information system report answers three questions quickly: how did we do, where did cash go and what needs attention.
metaTitle: What Is a Good MIS Report? Contents and Examples
metaDescription: What a monthly MIS report should include: profit and loss, balance sheet, cash flow, KPIs and commentary, and how a one-page summary helps owners decide faster.
body:
MIS stands for management information system. In practice, an MIS is the monthly report pack that tells owners and managers how the business is doing. Many MIS reports fail because they are too long, too late or too hard to read.

## What a good MIS answers

1. **How did we do?** Revenue, gross margin and profit against last month and against budget.
2. **Where did the cash go?** Cash balance, receivables, payables and any big movements.
3. **What needs attention?** A short list of exceptions, risks and decisions.

## What to include

- A one-page summary with the headline numbers and three to five lines of commentary.
- Profit and loss, balance sheet and cash flow in a standard layout.
- Key indicators that fit your business: gross margin, receivable days, cash runway, revenue by product or location.
- Variance against budget or prior period, with explanations for the big movements.

## What to skip

- Pages of ledger detail that nobody reads.
- Metrics with no owner or no decision attached.
- Charts that repeat the table next to them.

## Timing matters

A MIS delivered on the 7th is far more useful than a perfect one delivered on the 25th. Fix the date, then improve the content.

## Live dashboards

A dashboard link that opens on a phone gives you the numbers between reports. It should show the same figures as the monthly pack, so there is only one version of the truth.
